title: Liaison — Linking Sounds (연음)
plainEnglish: When a syllable ends in a consonant and the next starts with ㅇ (a vowel), that consonant slides over to begin the next syllable.
whenToUse: This happens constantly in speech: 한국어 sounds like 한구거, 음악이 like 으마기, 꽃이 like 꼬치. The spelling never changes — only the sound links.
attachmentRule: A final consonant (받침) before an ㅇ-initial syllable moves to become that syllable's onset: 꽃 + 이 → [꼬치], 음악 + 을 → [으마글], 옷 + 이 → [오시], 한국 + 어 → [한구거]. A double 받침 splits — one stays, one moves: 읽 + 어 → [일거], 앉 + 아 → [안자]. Liaison does not cross a clear pause between words.
contrastWith: You still WRITE 꽃이, 음악을, 한국어 — only the pronunciation links. This is the #1 reason Korean sounds different from how it looks on the page.

examples.en: The flowers are really pretty. (sounds like 꼬치)
I listen to music. (sounds like 으마글)
The clothes are too small. (sounds like 오시)

commonMistakes: Pronouncing each block separately (꼳-이 instead of 꼬치).
Forgetting a double 받침 splits: 읽어요 is [일거요], not [익어요].
studyOrder: Spot a 받침 followed by ㅇ
Slide the 받침 into the next syllable
For double 받침, keep one and move one
beginnerExplanation: Korean is written in neat syllable blocks, but in speech a final consonant 'jumps' onto the next block when that block starts with a vowel (the silent ㅇ). So 한국어 is read 한구거, and 꽃이 is read 꼬치. You keep spelling it the normal way — only the sound links up. Once you expect this, listening gets much easier.

title: Nasalization (비음화)
plainEnglish: A stop consonant (ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ) turns into a nasal (ㅇ/ㄴ/ㅁ) when the next syllable starts with ㄴ or ㅁ.
whenToUse: Why 감사합니다 sounds like 감사함니다 and 학년 like 항년. It happens whenever a stop 받침 bumps into ㄴ or ㅁ.
attachmentRule: Before ㄴ or ㅁ: a ㄱ-type 받침 (ㄱㄲㅋㄳㄺ) → ㅇ (학년 → [항년], 국물 → [궁물]); a ㄷ-type 받침 (ㄷㅅㅆㅈㅊㅌㅎ) → ㄴ (받는 → [반는], 옛날 → [옌날]); a ㅂ-type 받침 (ㅂㅍㄼㄿ) → ㅁ (입니다 → [임니다], 앞문 → [암문]).
contrastWith: Spelling stays the same (입니다, 학년). This is different from liaison: nasalization happens before ㄴ/ㅁ, while liaison happens before a vowel (ㅇ).

examples.en: I'm in third grade. (학년 sounds like 항년)
The broth is hot. (국물 sounds like 궁물)
This is Korean food. (입니다 sounds like 임니다)

commonMistakes: Pronouncing the hard 합니다 as written instead of [함니다].
Missing it in -습니다/-ㅂ니다 endings, which always nasalize to [-슴니다]/[-ㅁ니다].
studyOrder: Find a ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ 받침 before ㄴ or ㅁ
beginnerExplanation: Some 받침 sounds soften when they run into ㄴ or ㅁ. A ㄱ-sound becomes ㅇ (학년 → 항년), a ㄷ-sound becomes ㄴ (받는 → 반는), and a ㅂ-sound becomes ㅁ (입니다 → 임니다). That's why the polite -습니다 ending is pronounced -슴니다. You don't change the spelling — just the sound.

title: Palatalization (구개음화)
plainEnglish: A final ㄷ or ㅌ turns into ㅈ or ㅊ when the next sound is 이 (or 히).
whenToUse: Why 같이 is pronounced 가치 and 굳이 is 구지. It only happens with ㄷ/ㅌ + 이.
attachmentRule: When a 받침 ㄷ/ㅌ meets the vowel 이: ㄷ + 이 → 지 (굳이 → [구지], 해돋이 → [해도지], 맏이 → [마지]); ㅌ + 이 → 치 (같이 → [가치], 끝이 → [끄치], 붙이다 → [부치다]). With 히 it also applies: 닫히다 → [다치다].
contrastWith: This is a special case of liaison: normally ㅌ + 이 would just link to [티], but before 이 the sound shifts forward in the mouth to [치]. Only ㄷ/ㅌ do this, and only before 이/히.

examples.en: Shall we go together? (같이 sounds like 가치)
You don't have to come (no need). (굳이 sounds like 구지)
I can't see the end. (끝이 sounds like 끄치)
I stick on a sticker. (붙여 area, 붙이- → 부치-)

commonMistakes: Reading 같이 as [가티] — before 이 it becomes [가치].
Over-applying it: it only affects ㄷ/ㅌ before 이/히, not other consonants or vowels.
studyOrder: Spot a ㄷ or ㅌ 받침 right before 이/히
Remember the common word 같이 → 가치
beginnerExplanation: When ㄷ or ㅌ at the end of a syllable meets 이, the sound slides forward and becomes ㅈ or ㅊ. So 같이 ('together') is said 가치, and 굳이 is 구지. It's a small rule, but 같이 is such a common word that getting it right (가치, not 가티) makes you sound much more natural.

title: Aspiration (격음화)
plainEnglish: ㅎ merges with a neighboring ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ/ㅈ to make the strong, breathy ㅋ/ㅌ/ㅍ/ㅊ.
whenToUse: Why 좋다 sounds like 조타 and 축하해요 like 추카해요. It works in either order (ㅎ before or after the stop).
attachmentRule: ㅎ + ㄱ (or ㄱ + ㅎ) → ㅋ: 축하 → [추카], 그렇게 → [그러케]. ㅎ + ㄷ → ㅌ: 좋다 → [조타], 많다 → [만타]. ㅎ + ㅂ → ㅍ: 입학 → [이팍], 잡히다 → [자피다]. ㅎ + ㅈ → ㅊ: 좋지 → [조치], 맞히다 → [마치다]. ㅅ-type 받침 + 해 also works: 못해 → [모태].
contrastWith: The two plain sounds fuse into ONE aspirated sound — you don't hear ㅎ separately. Compare plain 다 vs aspirated 타 in 좋다 → [조타].

examples.en: The weather is really nice. (좋다 sounds like 조타)
I can't do that. (못해 sounds like 모태)
I entered university. (입학 sounds like 이팍)

commonMistakes: Trying to pronounce ㅎ as a separate sound — 좋다 is one fused [조타], not [조ㅎ다].
Missing it in 못해/안 해도 — 못해 is [모태].
studyOrder: Find a ㅎ next to ㄱ/ㄷ/ㅂ/ㅈ (either order)
Practice 좋다 → 조타 and 축하 → 추카
beginnerExplanation: The letter ㅎ is 'breathy', and when it touches ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ, or ㅈ, the two fuse into one strong aspirated sound: ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ, ㅊ. So 좋다 is said 조타, 축하 is 추카, and 못해 is 모태. You won't hear the ㅎ on its own — it gets absorbed into the harder sound.
